data.name: Indra
data.gender_notes: Indra is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: King of the gods; the mighty one
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root ind, 'to be powerful' — Indra, 'the mighty one'. Its root is Sanskrit ind (इन्द्). Indra, the Vedic king of the gods. Indra is a Sanskrit name meaning “King of the gods; the mighty one”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Indra expresses “King of the gods; the mighty one”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root ind, 'to be powerful' — Indra, 'the mighty one'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Indra total 28, reducing to 1. Number 1 is associated with leadership, independence and initiative.

vedic_reference.note: Indra is the king of gods and the god of rain and thunder in Hinduism. He is mentioned in the Rigveda and other ancient Hindu texts. He is considered the god of strength and is invoked for success and victory.

historical_references.reference: Indra, the Vedic king of the gods.
